assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: Small gold particles and arrows pass through a central membrane channel; a larger purple particle remains on one side.
assets.alt: Small gold particles and arrows pass through a central membrane channel; a larger purple particle remains on one side.
assets.caption: Selective transport: a channel allows a particular substance through. The larger particle is not shown crossing. Real selectivity depends on charge, chemistry, size and transport proteins, not size alone. This is not a literal two-wall membrane section.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: A large purple circular nucleus contains a dark nucleolus and a winding strand.
assets.alt: A large purple circular nucleus contains a dark nucleolus and a winding strand.
assets.caption: A nucleus contains most DNA in typical plant and animal cells. The winding strand represents chromatin, not a literal enlarged single chromosome. Nuclear pores and the double envelope are simplified; mitochondria and chloroplasts also contain DNA.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: An orange oval organelle contains a repeatedly folded internal line.
assets.alt: An orange oval organelle contains a repeatedly folded internal line.
assets.caption: A mitochondrion has a folded inner membrane supporting reactions that produce ATP during aerobic respiration. It transforms chemical energy rather than creating energy. The folds are schematic, not a measured section.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: An oval cell outlined in teal contains a purple nucleus, orange folded mitochondria, small dark ribosomes and a small blue compartment.
assets.alt: An oval cell outlined in teal contains a purple nucleus, orange folded mitochondria, small dark ribosomes and a small blue compartment.
assets.caption: Typical animal-cell model: teal membrane surrounds pale cytoplasm, with nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes and other compartments. There is no cell wall or chloroplast. Real cell shapes vary, and specialized cells can lack parts shown here.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: Two purple ribosome subunits straddle a teal strand while a gold bead chain emerges nearby.
assets.alt: Two purple ribosome subunits straddle a teal strand while a gold bead chain emerges nearby.
assets.caption: A ribosome reads messenger RNA and assembles an amino-acid chain that becomes a protein. Teal represents RNA and gold beads amino acids. These symbols and proportions are simplified.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: Two equally sized brown cell walls contain a large blue water-filled compartment at left and a smaller one at right.
assets.alt: Two equally sized brown cell walls contain a large blue water-filled compartment at left and a smaller one at right.
assets.caption: Qualitative water-loss comparison: a hydrated cell has turgor; water loss reduces vacuole volume and pressure against the wall. Severe water loss can pull the membrane inward, as exaggerated at right. Wilting has other possible causes too.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: A green oval organelle contains three stacks of flattened green discs.
assets.alt: A green oval organelle contains three stacks of flattened green discs.
assets.caption: Chloroplast thylakoid membranes contain chlorophyll and support light-driven reactions. Carbon fixation occurs in the surrounding stroma. Photosynthetic plant cells also contain mitochondria; making sugars and transferring energy from them are different processes.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: A rectangular plant-cell model has a brown wall, teal inner membrane, large blue vacuole, purple nucleus, green chloroplasts and orange mitochondria.
assets.alt: A rectangular plant-cell model has a brown wall, teal inner membrane, large blue vacuole, purple nucleus, green chloroplasts and orange mitochondria.
assets.caption: Typical photosynthetic plant-cell model. The outer brown wall supports a separate teal membrane; the blue central vacuole is large. Green chloroplasts and orange mitochondria have different jobs. Many plant cells, including onion bulb epidermis, lack chloroplasts. Colors and scale are schematic.

assets.prompt: Exact text-free scientific diagram: Purple folded membranes connect by a vesicle and arrows to gold curved stacks and a small outgoing vesicle.
assets.alt: Purple folded membranes connect by a vesicle and arrows to gold curved stacks and a small outgoing vesicle.
assets.caption: For many secreted and membrane proteins, ribosomes on rough ER assemble proteins, transport vesicles carry them to Golgi, and Golgi modifies and sorts them. Not every protein follows this route. Smooth ER also has roles in lipid synthesis and other functions.
